title: I built a blender plugin that batch exports sprite sheets in up to 16 directions.
author: Defiant_Medicine_823
selftext:
I've always been fascinated by how good diablo 2's graphics looked for that era so I embarked on a quest to replicate the process, but much quicker. I can now generate a 3D model, animate it and batch process multiple animations in 16 directions in under 30 minutes. Eventually I will make the tool public, but for now I am using it to build my own game. I'm posting this because I'm curious if anyone is else has tried this and to what level of success. 

  
For those curious I use:

\>Hunyuan3d for the models

\>Accurig for rigging and animations

\>Blender for the rendering and spritesheets packing 

Then I built a addon for Godot that bundles all the spritesheets into one file.

replies.author: SidAkrita
replies.body:
TLDR : just a scene in Godot that I launch with the mesh I want to capture.  
  
For now it's just a scene with a camera, some lights, and the mesh I want to create pngs from. I have 2 viewports, one with the 3D nodes (cam, lights, mesh...) and one with a TextureRect with a custom shader to apply pixelisation, dithering and so on. The camera sends its output to this TextureRect.

When I launch the scene, I play each animation frame from the mesh's AnimationPlayer one by one, and save the output of the TextureRect in a png, using viewport().get\_texture().get\_image() and saving it to a png file.

After that I just have a bunch of png that I have to put manually in an AnimatedSprite3D, but the big part of the job is already done.
